name: Audit a prospect's website with Bright Data and GPT-5.6 and download the report

parameters.content:
## Audit a prospect's site and download a report with your name on it

The twenty minutes you spend checking a prospect's site before a pitch, done in one. The output is a **self-contained HTML file** you save and send, branded with your agency name.

### How it works

Give it the prospect's URL and your agency name. It fetches the home page plus the key pages you list, as **raw HTML** rather than markdown, because an audit needs exactly the parts markdown throws away: the title tag, the meta description, the canonical, image alt attributes, the viewport, structured data.

Each page is checked against a fixed list, and every check reports pass, fail or not applicable **with the value it actually found**. `robots.txt` is fetched separately - a stray `Disallow: /` promoted from staging is the most expensive mistake on this list and the one that wins the meeting.

GPT-5.6 writes the summary from the counted findings only. The report is assembled as HTML, converted to a file, and handed back as a download when the run finishes. Every audit is also written to a Data Table, so re-running it in three months shows what changed.

### Setup

1. Bright Data: a Web Unlocker zone as a Header Auth credential.

2. An OpenAI credential.

3. A Data Table called `site_audits` with columns `site`, `score`, `pages_checked`, `failing_checks` and `audited_at`. It will not add missing ones.

4. In **Settings**, put your agency name and the paths worth checking.

## 1. Who are we auditing
The prospect and your agency name. The name goes at the top of the file you send, so this is a report from you, not from a tool.

## 2. One page at a time
The loop's second output fetches a page as raw HTML and the parser sends it back. Output zero fires once every page is done.

## 3. The file that decides everything
robots.txt is small and nearly always there. A Disallow slash promoted from staging removes the whole domain from search, and it is the finding that wins the meeting.

## 4. Count, do not editorialise
Findings are rolled up by check, so the report says three of four pages rather than repeating itself. The model only ever sees numbers.

## 5. An opening a stranger will read
Leads with what costs them most, names the number behind it, and one line on what is already fine. An audit that is all criticism gets deleted.

## 6. Assemble it, keep it, hand it over
Self-contained HTML with inline styles, because it is opened from a downloads folder with no server behind it. The Data Table keeps every audit for the re-run.

## It reads the HTML, so it cannot see what JavaScript builds

Everything here is measured on the HTML the server returns. On a React or Vue site rendered entirely in the browser, the title and meta tags are usually still in the served HTML - frameworks put them there on purpose - but body content and internal links often are not.

So on a heavy single-page app, treat a low word count or a thin link list as **unknown rather than as a finding**. Sending a prospect an audit that says they have no content, when they have plenty, ends the conversation rather than starting it.

The tag-level checks - title, description, canonical, robots, viewport, alt text, structured data - are reliable either way, and they are the ones worth leading with.
